summary: The note surveys emerging multicultural artists who use mixed media to construct and express multifaceted identities, blending traditions, materials and political messages. It profiles several artists and their 2023 exhibitions, including Jia Min Lee, Carlos Enriquez Gonzalez, Zahra Al-Mahdi, Tayo Oke and Maria Alvarez. It also discusses cultural hybridity, globalization, community engagement, and the expected growth of this art movement.
one_line: Emerging multicultural artists use mixed media to explore identity, migration, colonialism and globalization, as shown in several 2023 exhibitions and community projects.
key_facts: Jia Min Lee, a Korean immigrant, hosted her first major exhibition on October 12, 2023.
Jia Min Lee's canvases use layers of rice paper and acrylic infused with urban graffiti motifs to examine migration and integration.
Carlos Enriquez Gonzalez unveiled his work on September 15, 2023, at an avant-garde Los Angeles gallery, drawing on his Venezuelan roots.
Carlos Enriquez Gonzalez embeds traditional weavings with shards of clear plastic to critique cultural erosion and environmental degradation.
Zahra Al-Mahdi's exhibition opened on November 4, 2023, addressing the female Middle Eastern experience against western perceptions.
Zahra Al-Mahdi combines video art, 3D printing and traditional embroidery to create immersive installations about Arab women, culture and veiling.
Nigerian-born Tayo Oke presented an exhibition in December 2023 on the aftermath of colonialism.
Tayo Oke's sculptures combine repurposed colonial artifacts with traditional African symbols to address historical wounds and cultural reclamation.
Maria Alvarez staged a collaborative mural in downtown Miami on September 20, 2023, involving local schools and cultural institutions.
Maria Alvarez said of the mural: "It's about weaving our stories together, our struggles, our dreams."
The note argues that identity is not a static construct but a fluid amalgamation of influences that shifts over time.
Many of these artists arrange workshops, talks and collaborative projects with local communities to foster shared heritage.
